title: Port Scanners
description: Who is scanning the network: TCP connection attempts that fan out across many targets or services and never complete, ICMP sweeps, and Suricata's own scan signatures. Click a source to see exactly which ports and hosts it tried and which answered.

panels.title: Scanning Sources
panels.description: Sources whose TCP connection attempts reach many targets or many services AND almost never complete (FIN/SYN under 20%). That combination is what a port scan is; a busy legitimate client fans out just as wide but finishes its connections. The count is of hosts, over the dashboard range.

targets.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"
import "array"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

// Connection attempts: flows that carried a SYN. A flow without one is the
// continuation of a connection cut by active_timeout=5, not a new attempt.
opens = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r.protocol == "6" and r._field == "syn_packets" and r._value > 0)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip", "service"])
  |> count()

// Handshake outcome per source. SYN is counted in both directions (SYN and
// SYN-ACK), and so is FIN, so a completed connection reads syn 2 / fin 2.
flags = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r.protocol == "6" and (r._field == "syn_packets" or r._field == "fin_packets" or r._field == "rst_packets"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "_field"])
  |> sum()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: r._field, v: r._value}))

found = union(tables: [
  opens |> group(columns: ["src_ip"]) |> sum()
        |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: "attempts", v: r._value})),
  opens |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"]) |> sum() |> group(columns: ["src_ip"]) |> count()
        |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: "targets", v: r._value})),
  opens |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "service"]) |> sum() |> group(columns: ["src_ip"]) |> count()
        |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: "services", v: r._value})),
  flags,
])
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["src_ip"], columnKey: ["k"], valueColumn: "v")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.attempts and r.attempts >= ${min_attempts})
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.targets >= 20 or r.services >= 5)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with
      completion: if r.syn_packets > 0 then float(v: r.fin_packets) / float(v: r.syn_packets) * 100.0 else 0.0,
      refused: float(v: r.rst_packets) / float(v: r.attempts) * 100.0,
      pattern: if r.targets >= 20 and r.services >= 5 then "block"
               else if r.services >= 5 then "vertical" else "horizontal"}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with
      verdict: if r.completion < 20.0 then "SCAN" else if r.completion < 50.0 then "CHECK" else "BUSY CLIENT"}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.verdict == "SCAN")
  |> count(column: "src_ip")
  |> rename(columns: {src_ip: "_value"})

// Union a zero so an empty result reads NONE rather than a blank tile.
union(tables: [found, array.from(rows: [{_value: 0}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()

panels.title: Suricata Scan Alerts
panels.description: IDS alerts from the ET SCAN signatures (or category 'Detection of a Network Scan') in range. Independent of the flow heuristics on this board, so the two corroborate each other. Details in the Suricata dashboard.

panels.title: TCP Attempts Seen
panels.description: Every flow in range that carried a SYN. This tile exists so that NONE on its neighbours means 'nothing scanned', not 'no data': if it reads NO FLOWS, the collector is not writing, and the other tiles prove nothing.

panels.title: Scan Candidates (click a source to drill down)
panels.description: Every source with at least $min_attempts TCP connection attempts that reached 20+ distinct targets (horizontal) or 5+ distinct services (vertical) in range. Services are the collector's bucketed dst_port, so a 1-1000 port scan shows as ~30 services, not 1000 -- the exact ports are in the drill-down. Completion is FIN/SYN over all of the source's TCP: a real client finishes its connections (~100%), a scan does not (~0%). Refused is RSTs per attempt -- high for a scan of closed ports, low for one against filtered ones. Known scanners (vulnerability scanners, monitoring) will appear here every time; that is expected. Country is from a local GeoIP database (IP geolocation by DB-IP, db-ip.com); "private network" for any non-public address.

panels.title: Connection Attempts per Candidate
panels.description: TCP connection attempts over time for the ten busiest scan candidates. A scan is a short, dense block; a busy client is a long, even band. The bucket follows the time range (~96 buckets, at least 1 minute) and is labelled with its start, so zooming onto a block selects the attempts that drew it.

targets.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

spanNs = int(v: v.timeRangeStop) - int(v: v.timeRangeStart)
everyNs = if spanNs / 96 < 60000000000 then 60000000000 else spanNs / 96
every = duration(v: everyNs)

attempts = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r.protocol == "6" and r._field == "syn_packets" and r._value > 0)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ /^${scanners:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])

// The ten busiest candidates only: ten colours is what a legend can still map
// back to a host. contains() runs on the per-source totals, not on raw rows.
top = attempts
  |> count()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 10)
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "src_ip")

attempts
  |> aggregateWindow(every: every, fn: count, timeSrc: "_start", createEmpty: false)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r.src_ip, set: top))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "src_ip"])

panels.description: What the candidates were looking for: distinct (service, target) pairs the scan candidates tried, per service. smb, rdp, ssh and telnet at the top is the classic lateral-movement search.

panels.title: Router Scanner List
panels.description: Whether mikrotik-responder is putting detected scanners on the routers' `port-scanners` address list, and how many distinct sources it listed in the selected range. LISTING: the same SCAN verdict as the table above runs every scanners.interval_seconds over the last scanners.window_minutes, plus repeated ET/GPL SCAN alerts. OFF: scanners.enabled = false, or no router has the `scanners` role. QUERY FAILING: the verdict query errors (see the responder log). The list blocks nothing until a router rule references it (`python3 install.py --check` prints it). External sources only unless scanners.scope = all.

targets.query:
import "array"

// scan_watch is written by mikrotik-responder on every run of the scanner
// verdict; nothing in the last 15 minutes means it is not running there --
// scanners.enabled = false. DETECT ONLY (1): it runs, but no router takes
// the `scanners` role, so SCAN sources are recorded and alerted, not listed.
state = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "scan_watch" and r._field == "state_code")
  |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])
state_or_off = union(tables: [state, array.from(rows: [{_value: -1}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _field: "state"}))

listed = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "suricata_block" and r._field == "count")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.list == "port-scanners" and (r.result == "added" or r.result == "refreshed"))
  |> group(columns: ["ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> count()
listed_or_zero = union(tables: [listed, array.from(rows: [{_value: 0}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _field: "listed"}))

union(tables: [state_or_off, listed_or_zero])
  |> pivot(rowKey: [], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")

panels.title: Listed on the Routers (click a source to drill down)
panels.description: Every write to the `port-scanners` address list, one row per router. 'Why' is the flow verdict (attempts, targets, services, how many completed) or the ET SCAN signature that put the source there. A refresh is a source that kept scanning and had its RouterOS timeout pushed out. Uses the default list name; if scanners.list is changed, this table and the tile beside it need the same name.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "suricata_block" and r.list == "port-scanners")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 100)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "router", "ip", "result", "signature", "timeout"])

panels.title: Ports Tried by ${scanner}
panels.description: Exact destination ports this source tried in range, open ones first (up to 200). Outcome is read from the flow: 3+ packets means the target answered the SYN (open, or at least reachable), fewer packets with a RST means closed, fewer packets without one means nothing answered (filtered, or no such host). Empty until a source is chosen: click one in any table above, or type it in the Scanner box.

panels.title: Targets Tried by ${scanner}
panels.description: Hosts this source tried to connect to in range, the ones that answered first (up to 200). An Open count on a host is what the scan found. Outcome is read from the flow: 3+ packets means the target answered the SYN (open, or at least reachable), fewer packets with a RST means closed, fewer packets without one means nothing answered (filtered, or no such host). Empty until a source is chosen: click one in any table above, or type it in the Scanner box.

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict every panel to traffic with either endpoint in this range, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16, 10.12.6.0/24, or a bare IP. Leave empty for no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary, so /20 behaves as /16 and may show a wider range than typed.

list.name: min_attempts
list.label: Min. attempts
list.description: How many TCP connection attempts (flows carrying a SYN) a source needs in range before it is considered at all. Raise it on a busy network or a long range, lower it to catch slow scans.

list.name: scanner
list.label: Scanner
list.description: The source the drill-down at the bottom describes. Filled by clicking a source in any table; one IP, exactly.

list.name: scanners
list.label: Scan candidates (internal)
list.description: Hidden helper: the sources in the Scan Candidates table, fed to the reverse-DNS resolver and the per-candidate chart.
list.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

// Connection attempts: flows that carried a SYN. A flow without one is the
// continuation of a connection cut by active_timeout=5, not a new attempt.
opens = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r.protocol == "6" and r._field == "syn_packets" and r._value > 0)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip", "service"])
  |> count()

// Handshake outcome per source. SYN is counted in both directions (SYN and
// SYN-ACK), and so is FIN, so a completed connection reads syn 2 / fin 2.
flags = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r.protocol == "6" and (r._field == "syn_packets" or r._field == "fin_packets" or r._field == "rst_packets"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "_field"])
  |> sum()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: r._field, v: r._value}))

union(tables: [
  opens |> group(columns: ["src_ip"]) |> sum()
        |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: "attempts", v: r._value})),
  opens |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"]) |> sum() |> group(columns: ["src_ip"]) |> count()
        |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: "targets", v: r._value})),
  opens |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "service"]) |> sum() |> group(columns: ["src_ip"]) |> count()
        |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_ip: r.src_ip, k: "services", v: r._value})),
  flags,
])
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["src_ip"], columnKey: ["k"], valueColumn: "v")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.attempts and r.attempts >= ${min_attempts})
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.targets >= 20 or r.services >= 5)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with
      completion: if r.syn_packets > 0 then float(v: r.fin_packets) / float(v: r.syn_packets) * 100.0 else 0.0,
      refused: float(v: r.rst_packets) / float(v: r.attempts) * 100.0,
      pattern: if r.targets >= 20 and r.services >= 5 then "block"
               else if r.services >= 5 then "vertical" else "horizontal"}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with
      verdict: if r.completion < 20.0 then "SCAN" else if r.completion < 50.0 then "CHECK" else "BUSY CLIENT"}))
  |> sort(columns: ["attempts"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 25)
  |> keep(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> rename(columns: {src_ip: "_value"})
